text: This service reads payoff, collateral, encumbrance, customer, plan-status and freshness facts only through the rwb-source-data contract, and reads no ACE view and no ACE table.
why: Architecture v5 allows only rwb-source-data to read the 30 views and gives the S2 row no REST cell to P1, so the read path of the FSD cannot stand as written.
read: Arch v5 slides 37 and 45 (only rwb-source-data reads ACE), slide 13 (S2 row without a P1 cell), slide 18 (S2 contract), rules DP-05 and DP-13.
applied_in: FR-S2-004, FR-S2-007, FR-S2-017, AC-S2-002, AC-S2-023; section 2.4 item 1 and section 9
confirm: Solution architect with the P1 owner, before wave 3 system test
impact: An S2 to P1 REST cell has to be added to the connection matrix and to the contract; until then the offer has no agreed source.

text: The status a case held before the offer is held on the treatment, and the write back to the collections system is raised through the rwb-integration contract.
why: The FSD returns the case to COLLINS, which has no path from this service in Architecture v5.
read: Arch v5 slide 41 and slide 16 (P2 owns interface config and outbound items), rule DP-16, FSD S2 A2.9.
confirm: Solution architect with the integration lead, before wave 3 system test
impact: P2 owns the interface, its retries and its exception queue; this service owns the prior status and its reason.

text: This service owns the four entity groups that Architecture v5 names (treatments, contracts, settlement and deed in lieu agreements, plan timers) and the Ownership Map's single `treatment` row is read as the first of them.
why: The architecture gives four groups and the map gives one table, so the register is incomplete rather than the architecture wrong.
read: Arch v5 slide 18 and slide 41 (four entity groups), slide 30 (schema rwb_treatment), Ownership Map Tables (treatment, S2).
confirm: Data architect, before the S2 DB story
impact: The missing rows are added to the Ownership Map in the same change as the DB story; no physical name is fixed here.

text: The offer command is published as POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit, and slide 18's POST /treatments/{id}/offer is read as the same command.
why: Two sources name one operation differently, and the map's path is the one the API specification and the TSD carry.
read: Arch v5 slide 18 (POST /treatments/{id}/offer), Ownership Map Endpoints (POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/submit, S2, API Specification v4 and TSD S2 appendix T-A).
confirm: Solution architect, before the S2 contract story closes
impact: One path is fixed in the contract story; whether a GET /treatments list exists is carried as an open question.

text: TreatmentClosed is published on rwb.treatment.events.v1, keyed by caseId, as a CloudEvent through the outbox, and carries no EV number until the catalogue allocates one.
why: Slide 18 gives the event and slide 43 carries it only in the additional rows, while the map holds EV-10 TreatmentApproved alone.
read: Arch v5 slide 18 (EVT TreatmentApproved, TreatmentClosed), slide 43 row 10 and the additional rows, Ownership Map Events (EV-10 only).
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 system test
impact: rwb-case and rwb-reporting consume it; the numbering is the catalogue owner's.

text: The validity, credit approval and plan clocks are durable timers inside TreatmentWorkflow set through the workflow kit, and no Quartz table, job or connection is used.
why: Architecture v5 retires the shared Quartz tables and JOB-05, and the Temporal design runs every S2 clock in TreatmentWorkflow.
read: Arch v5 slide 44 (JOB-05 retired, durable timers), slide 20 (own Schedules), Temporal design slide 18 (TreatmentWorkflow, clocks 14 days, 30 days, 3 working days), rule DP-10.
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 3 system test
impact: A timer breach is reported on the case timer path that rwb-case owns; this service adds no Schedule.

text: Every treatment step runs inside TreatmentWorkflow, started by rwb-case, and by the events of the services that own the fact; this service adds no Schedule and no batch trigger.
why: The FSD's 'completed ACE batch' trigger is removed by D-RCV-35, AceDataReady does not reach this service, and the job map holds no S2 job.
read: Arch v5 slide 43 row 26 (AceDataReady consumers), slide 44 (job map, no S2 row), Program BRD v5 section 6.3, FSD S2 A2.x step 1.
confirm: Solution architect with the P1 owner, before the S2 contract story closes
impact: The moment each step runs is the workflow's own; a same-day trigger stays open under DL06.

text: Booking, payment matching and posting stay with rwb-payment; this service records the booking reference from TreatmentBooked and the break from PaymentMissed, and requests the posting and the release through the payment and integration contracts.
why: Architecture v5 gives rwb-payment the bookings, publishes TreatmentBooked and PaymentMissed, and gives this service those events as inputs, while the FSD writes them from this module.
read: Arch v5 slide 41 (P8 owns bookings and posting), slide 44 (JOB-07, JOB-08), slide 13 (S2 to P8 Temporal and events), Ownership Map Events (EV-11, EV-12).
confirm: Solution architect with the P8 owner, before wave 3 system test
impact: One writer of one booking; the rental and receipt loop is carried to a later increment and as an open question.

text: The treatment document set is requested through the rwb-document contract, the offer and notice dispatch happens on TreatmentApproved through rwb-comms, and every signature is requested and returned on the legal path; this service holds only the document reference.
why: Architecture v5 gives the documents to P5 and the notices, templates and signature requests to P6, the connection matrix gives this service a Temporal call to P5 and no cell to P6, and the FSD names one Workbench document hub.
read: Arch v5 slide 41 (P5 and P6), slide 16 (P5 IN/OUT), slide 17 (P6 IN/OUT), slide 13 (S2 row: T to P5, no cell to P6), Ownership Map Endpoints (generated documents, review, signature requests, signature result), Ownership Map Events (EV-10 consumed by P6).
confirm: Solution architect with the P5 and P6 owners, before wave 3 system test
impact: No document content is held in schema rwb_treatment; the template and the signed document stay with P5 and P6.

text: The CCMS collateral release and the Land Office title check are raised through the rwb-integration contract, and the asset take-on is requested from S5 rwb-asset through its contract; this service records the reference each returns.
why: No v5 connection carries these outside systems from S2, while the architecture gives the integration paths to P2 and the asset to S5.
read: Arch v5 slide 41 (P2 integration, S5 asset), slide 19 (S5 IN/OUT), slide 13 (S2 row), FSD S2 A2.12, A2.13 and A2.17.
confirm: Solution architect with the integration lead, before wave 3 system test
impact: Two cells have to be added to the connection matrix; the encumbrance and title facts are read through P1 as the ACE-ingested view.

text: Every approval limit is read from the versioned delegation table of rwb-access at run time, the level applied and the approver role are recorded on the treatment, and the module is tested with one documented test set until DL18 is answered.
why: The limits are P4 data, DL18 is open on the holders and the limits, and the design quotes two different sets of numbers.
read: Ownership Map Tables (delegation_limit, P4, ASM-A6-tables-4), Program BRD v5 DL18, Epic 2 BRD v3 DL18 and section 7.1, Temporal design slide 18 (DoA 2.1.1).
confirm: Risk with the product heads, before wave 3 release
impact: The two quoted sets are not reconciled here; the test set is named in the test evidence and replaced when DL18 closes.

text: The three packages are evaluated from the embedded Drools kit with the universal rules in force, the package and rule version are recorded on every treatment, and the package codes, labels and owners are named in rwb-decision before wave 3 release.
why: The design names three packages for this service and no source gives them a code, a label or an owner, while governance is central in P7.
read: Temporal design slide 18 (three packages in Phase 1, RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH, BOOKING_MATCH), Arch v5 slide 27 and slide 41 (P7 registry), Ownership Map Tables (rule_package, P7, ASM-A6-tables-3), rule DP-04.
confirm: Center of excellence analyst with P7, before wave 3 release
impact: A rule set without a version label cannot be promoted or tested; the module evaluates the universal package until the three are registered.

text: Each acceptance criterion of this PRD is written from the FSD's own step, rule and field catalog, and the FSD acceptance criterion ID is kept in the evidence column.
why: All eighteen FSD criteria are placeholders that state no observable outcome, so a criterion cannot be taken from them as written.
read: FSD S2 A2.1.4.1 to A2.18.4.1 (the placeholder rows), A2.1.4.2 to A2.18.4.4 (None), A2.1.3.1 to A2.18.3.1 (the rules), A2.2.3.2 (the field catalog).
confirm: Business analyst, S2, before wave 3 system test
impact: The FSD owner replaces the placeholders at the next FSD version and names the alternate flows and background events of the module.

text: Wave 2 delivers the published contract, the treatment record and the data date; wave 3 delivers the offers, the settlement, the plan, the deed in lieu, the documents and the release; both dates are copied as tentative.
why: The service is wave 2 and EP02 while every requirement of the module is an Epic 3 requirement, and no source says which capabilities the E2 release carries.
read: Arch v5 slide 41 (S2 wave 2), rules R5.6 (EP02 wave 2), Epic 2 BRD v3 sections 8.1 and 8.3 (31 December 2026 (tentative)), Program BRD v5 sections 5.9 and 8 (E3 31 January 2027 (tentative)), FSD S2 document control ('E2 foundations; E3').
confirm: Solution architect and the Product Owner, before wave 2 release
impact: No requirement changes; only the release a capability lands in, and the contract is what lets the other services build in wave 2.

text: MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-001 are served from the catalogues of the services that own them, and MSG-S2-001 is held in this service's catalogue with a Thai and an English version.
why: Four of the five messages belong to other services and DL10 is open on the Thai wording of every message.
read: FSD S2 VR-S2-001-1 to VR-S2-018-1 and A2.1.4.3 to A2.18.4.3, Ownership Map Services (P1, P4, P7), Program BRD v5 DL10.
confirm: Business analyst, S2, before wave 3 release
impact: No message of this service's own beyond MSG-S2-001; the wording of all five passes DL10 before wave 3 release.

text: The treatment, the agreements and the plan timers carry a classification from the working labels of this document (SENSITIVE_FINANCIAL for the terms and the agreements, CONFIDENTIAL for the references), and the retention period is stated as open.
why: NFR-047 and NFR-028 require a class and a period, the FSD marks all eight fields as not personal data, and DL26 holds both open.
read: Program BRD v5 NFR-047, NFR-028 and DL26, FSD S2 field catalog, Epic 2 BRD v3 section 7 DL26.
confirm: Compliance and PDPA officer, before wave 3 release
impact: The class sets handling now; the period is set under DL26 and the record class is named with it.

text: The eight catalog fields are required as written, and the contract, the agreement, the plan timer and the booking reference are required as records whose physical field list is open.
why: The FSD gives one eight-field catalog, twelve features have none, and Architecture v5 gives the schema four entity groups.
read: FSD S2 A2.2.3.2, A2.3.3.2, A2.4.3.2, A2.12.3.2, A2.15.3.2 (eight fields), Arch v5 slide 18 and slide 41 (four groups).
confirm: Data architect, before the S2 DB story
impact: No field is invented; the physical list is written with the DB story and no value is recomputed here.

text: Each prerequisite feature code of the FSD is read as the contract of the service that owns the capability, and the duplicate FEAT-CHO-08 is read as one dependency.
why: The FSD names feature codes of other modules, and the Ownership Map and the plan hold no feature code, so a dependency cannot be resolved from the FSD as written.
read: FSD S2 A1.1 and the prerequisite lines of A2.1 to A2.18, Ownership Map Services and Endpoints.
confirm: Solution architect, before the S2 contract story closes
impact: The mapping is recorded once in the service contract; no dependency is invented from a code the sources do not resolve.

text: This document stays at status Draft with an empty approval table, and the missing requirements approval is treated as an assumption rather than as an answer.
why: The governing BRDs are Draft with an empty approval table and the run records no human verification stop.
read: Epic 2 BRD v3 section 10.2 (empty approval table), rules R1 U8 (no human verification stop in this run).
confirm: Product Owner and FDA, after this run
impact: The gate is cleared outside this run; no approval is claimed here.

text: The inherited history carries FSD S2 version 3 in full, marks versions 1 and 2 as not specified, and reads the repeated FEAT-CHO-08 as one dependency.
why: The FSD change note describes only the step from v2 to v3 and the dependency sentence repeats a code.
read: FSD S2 document control (Version 3, 15 November 2026) and A1.1.
confirm: Business analyst, S2, at the next FSD version
impact: Two change notes are outstanding; nothing is reconstructed.

text: The live treatment row is this service's, and P1's `dp_treatment` is a dated read-only copy built from this service's events, never read here as the source of a treatment.
why: The Ownership Map gives `treatment` to S2 and `dp_treatment` to P1 with a ruling, so two tables with one name exist at the boundary.
read: Ownership Map Tables (treatment S2; dp_treatment P1, ASM-A6-tables-14), Arch v5 slide 18 and slide 41, slide 37 (data lake removed).
confirm: Data architect, before the S2 DB story
impact: One writer of the live record; reporting reads the copy and never writes it.

text: This is the first PRD of the S2 family, so version 1 is the next version and no earlier version is superseded.
why: The PRD folder held P1 to P10 and S1 and no S2 file before this run.
read: The PRD folder listing (eleven files, none of them S2).
confirm: Requirement owner role, at the next version
impact: No earlier version is edited and no history is reconstructed.

text: The release dates E2 31 December 2026 and E3 31 January 2027 are copied from the release plan and marked (tentative).
why: Rule U7 keeps every date unchanged and tentative.
read: Program BRD v5 section 8 (release plan), Epic 2 BRD v3 metadata and section 1.
confirm: Programme office, at each release
impact: No date is a gap and no date is raised.

text: This service's delivery wave (2) equals the wave of the business epic EP02 (2), so no wave conflict is raised between them; the difference between EP02 and the E3 release of the requirements is carried as a separate release-sequencing gap.
why: Rule R5.6 raises a conflict only where the business epic wave is earlier than the service wave, and here the two are equal.
read: Arch v5 slide 41 (S2 wave 2), rules R5.6 (EP02 wave 2), Epic 2 BRD v3 section 8.3.
confirm: Solution architect, before wave 2 release
impact: No conflict gap is raised for the two waves; the requirement release is carried by CG-B-REQ-PRD-S2-14.

text: Every owner named in this document is a role or a service code taken from the Ownership Map or the BRD, and no person is named anywhere.
why: Rule U3 forbids names of people and the BRD names roles.
read: Ownership Map Services and Rulings, Program BRD v5 requirement owners, Epic 2 BRD v3 sections 5 and 7.
confirm: Requirement owner role, at the next version
impact: Ownership is a suggestion by team type, and any team may pick a story up.

text: REQ-S2-001 to REQ-S2-010 are both the program requirement IDs and the FSD requirement IDs of this module, and the Epic 2 requirement keys (RWB-E2-nnn) are carried beside them as the second BR trace.
why: The FSD 'Requirements served' table repeats the program IDs, and the Epic 2 BRD uses its own keys for the same module.
read: Program BRD v5 section 5.9, FSD S2 'Requirements served', Epic 2 BRD v3 section 3 and section 9.
confirm: Business analyst, S2, at the next BRD version
impact: No ID is renumbered; the two sets are joined in the trace summary and no requirement is left without a functional requirement.
